designSummary: Interrupted time series with a common start in February 2027: 12 monthly baseline points and 14 monthly intervention points per ward, pooled across 12 wards.
sampleSize: Twelve wards with 26 monthly points each give 312 ward-months. With a baseline near 19 catheter days per 100 patient days and ward-to-ward variation of about 4, a pooled segmented regression can detect a level change of about 20 percent with 80 percent power, assuming modest autocorrelation; infections (about 2 per 1,000 catheter days) are too few for any test.
primaryAnalysis: Segmented Poisson regression of monthly catheter days with patient days as the offset, a common change point in February 2027, ward random effects and a first-order autoregressive term.
secondaryAnalysis: Descriptive infection rates; run charts of indication documentation and reinsertion.
missingData: Months with incomplete flowsheet extracts are flagged and excluded from the model; no imputation.
multiplicity: One primary measure; secondary and balancing measures are descriptive.
software: R; code archived before the first start.
summary: Pooled segmented regression with one common change point.
